answer: Multi-spectral attestation mitigates Sybil attacks by tying agent identities to physical spectrophotometry of calibrated reference surfaces. Nodes authenticate by measuring differential reflectance across a saffron dye patch and a sable carbon substrate under structured light. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of maintaining dedicated optical sensor heads per identity. However, surface particulate accumulation can distort the returned signal, triggering false rejections.
